title: Cap. VI Arg. 9 close: Christ and Christian infants not from foresight — nor the rest
pass_a_gloss: But Grevinchovius perhaps meant this, that all infants are saved indiscriminately, and therefore that there is no election of infants. But against this one unsound disputant I set the judgment of the catholic Church, which always felt that all infants are born children of wrath, but that not all are reborn, but those alone whom God dignifies with unowed grace. The sum is: Christ is not predestinated from any foresight of merits; nor the infants of Christians: Therefore neither the remaining Christians, of all of whom the election is of one kind and of the same ratio with the election of their Head, and among themselves.
pass_b_english: Or Grevinchovius meant all infants are saved alike, so there is no infant election. Against that one unsound disputant stands the catholic Church's judgment: all infants are born children of wrath; not all are reborn — only those God dignifies with unowed grace. Sum: Christ is not predestined from foresight of merits; nor Christian infants. Therefore neither are the remaining Christians — whose election is of one kind and the same ratio with their Head's, and among themselves.
source_text: Sed Grevinchovius fortasse id voluit, omnes infantes salvari promiscue, ac proinde nullam esse electionem infantium. Sed huic uni malesano disputatori oppono catholicae Ecclesiae judicium, quae semper sensit omnes infantes nasci filios irae, renasci autem non omnes, sed illos solos quos Deus indebita gratia dignatur. Summa est: Christus non est praedestinatus ex aliqua praevisione meritorum; neque infantes Christianorum: Ergo nec reliqui Christiani, quorum omnium electio est uniusmodi et ejusdem rationis cum electione sui Capitis, et inter se.
